functions.name: psContour
functions.signature:
void psContour (float c, int nx, float x[], int ny, float y[], float z[],
		float lcs, char *lcf, char *lcc, float *w, int nplaces);
functions.purpose: Trace and optionally label a contour of a two-dimensional grid using PostScript.
functions.float_sensitive_notes: Contour traversal and label placement depend on comparison boundaries, interpolation, traversal order, and updates to w; unsuffixed constants introduce double arithmetic in some expressions. The function and its static helpers alter the two least significant bits of float grid values through int-pointer casts, which are explicitly described as nonportable and also raise C aliasing concerns. Static helpers emit PostScript through gsave, newpath, stroke, moveto, lineto, grestore, setcolor, rectfill, setfont, rotate, and show.

functions.name: psDrawCurve
functions.signature:
void psDrawCurve(
	float x, float y, float width, float height,
	float x1Beg, float x1End, float p1Beg, float p1End,
	float x2Beg, float x2End, float p2Beg, float p2End,
	float *x1curve, float *x2curve, int ncurve,
	char *curveColor, float curvewidth, int curvedash, int style);
functions.purpose: Transform, clip, and draw a styled curve within a PostScript axes box.
functions.float_sensitive_notes: Float scale and bias calculations and their evaluation order determine transformed coordinates; dash lengths are multiplied by the line width before drawing. Zero axis ranges can cause division by zero.
functions.license_note: Attributed to Brian Macy of Phillips Petroleum Co.; adapted after Dave Hale and others' psAxesBox routine.

functions.name: psLegendBox
functions.signature:
void psLegendBox(
	float x, float y, float width, float height,
	float x1Beg, float x1End, float p1Beg, float p1End,
	float d1Num, float f1Num, int n1Tic, int grid1, char *label1,
	char *labelFont, float labelSize,
	char *axesColor, char *gridColor,
	int style);
functions.purpose: Draw a PostScript legend box with a labeled axis, ticks, and optional grid.
functions.float_sensitive_notes: Number and tick loops repeatedly accumulate float increments, so rounding can affect loop endpoints and displayed ticks. log10 and pow operate in double precision with results stored in float; formatting and exponent-selection thresholds can change labels near boundaries. Invalid or zero increments and tick counts can cause division by zero or nonterminating loops.

functions.name: psLegendBBox
functions.purpose: Estimate an integer bounding box for a PostScript legend box.
functions.float_sensitive_notes: Expressions mix float values with double literals, then use the local IROUND macro or direct conversion to int; results near integer and half-integer boundaries depend on the specified evaluation and conversion behavior.

functions.name: psWiggle
functions.signature:
void psWiggle (
	int n, float z[], float zmin, float zmax, float zbase,
	float yzmin, float yzmax, float xfirst, float xlast, int ifill,
	const char *tracecolor);
functions.purpose: Draw a clipped seismic wiggle trace with optional solid and gray area fills.
functions.float_sensitive_notes: The routine processes overlapping segments and uses exact equality at the fill baseline and a float tolerance to suppress line segments; clipping intersections and operation order affect output. Unsuffixed constants can promote expressions to double, and static scratch arrays make concurrent calls unsafe.
